page: Amazon Web Services g4ad.xlarge is a graphics-focused virtual server powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7R32 processor operating at 3.0 GHz, configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs from 2 physical cores with multithreading. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For graphics acceleration, it includes a single AMD Radeon Pro Navi V520 GPU with 8 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage is provided by a 150 GB NVMe SSD, and baseline network bandwidth is rated at 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate modest CPU and memory performance. The single-core and multi-core stress-ng CPU tests place the instance in the bottom 10% of performance tiers. Memory bandwidth tests for both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks fall into the bottom 25% tier, though Passmark memory scores and single-threaded gzip compression achieve middle 50% average ratings. Geekbench multi-core, ray tracing, and image processing benchmarks also rank in the bottom 25%. For machine learning workloads, LLM text generation using a small 135M model reaches an average speed of 103.47 tokens per second, but drops to a poor 5.34 tokens per second on a medium 7B model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the g4ad.xlarge offers a specialized hardware profile that bundles dedicated GPU acceleration and local NVMe storage on a modest 4-vCPU footprint. This resource density makes it a qualitative option for workloads requiring hardware-accelerated graphics or basic virtual desktop infrastructure without the overhead of larger compute instances. The hardware is best suited for entry-level graphics rendering, remote workstation hosting, and lightweight GPU-accelerated tasks, whereas heavy multi-threaded compute or high-throughput database operations are limited by the lower CPU and memory bandwidth performance.
